Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] TeamPCP Checkmarx KICS supply-chain stealer C2 callback (audit.checkmarx.cx / 94.154.172.43) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Kubernetes API curl/wget with ServiceAccount token from container · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] TeamPCP Checkmarx KICS supply-chain stealer C2 callback (audit.checkmarx.cx / 94.154.172.43) Command & Control High
Catches the post-compromise C2 beacon from the TeamPCP-poisoned KICS Docker image. Network egress to the hardcoded domain audit.checkmarx.cx or the IP 94.154.172.43 from any host running the tainted KICS scanner container. Rationale: Anchors on the exact IP 94.154.172.43 and FQDN audit.checkmarx.cx pre-extracted from the article — the TeamPCP-controlled C2 the KICS stealer talks to during scanning. High-fidelity because these are not generic infrastructure; only an org talking to Checkmarx KICS would even conceivably resolve audit.checkmarx.cx and that domain isn't on any legitimate Checkmarx documentation page (cross-check vs vendor).

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url

[LLM] Privileged container launch — docker run --privileged from non-CI parent Exploitation Medium
Detects docker / podman / nerdctl invocations carrying --privileged when the parent is not a known container runtime or CI runner. Privileged containers disable nearly all isolation primitives (all capabilities granted, full /dev access, no seccomp) and are the most common pre-condition for container escape in the article. Rationale: Anchors on the exact `--privileged` flag and `docker exec` strings quoted as code blocks in the article. The CI-parent exclusion catches the legitimate use cases (buildkitd, gitlab/jenkins/github runners) and keeps the alert focused on interactive-shell or unexpected-parent invocations, which is where supply-chain compromise or insider misuse shows up.
ATT&CKT1611 T1610
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("docker","podman","nerdctl")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--privileged"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (" run "," create "," exec ")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("containerd-shim","buildkitd","kubelet","Runner.Listener","gitlab-runner","jenkins","github-runner"))
| where not(InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("jenkins","gitlab-runner","github-runner","buildkite-agent"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("docker","podman","nerdctl") or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\b(docker|podman|nerdctl)\b"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "--privileged"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (" run "," create "," exec ")
| where not(ParentProcessName has_any ("containerd-shim","buildkitd","kubelet","Runner.Listener","gitlab-runner","jenkins","github-runner"))
| where not(ActorUsername in~ ("jenkins","gitlab-runner","github-runner","buildkite-agent"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Container escape via cgroups release_agent write (CVE-2022-0492) Exploitation High
Detects file writes to a release_agent path under /sys/fs/cgroup — the exact primitive abused by CVE-2022-0492 to escape a container and execute arbitrary commands on the host. Pairs the write with the canonical follow-up notify_on_release setting. Rationale: CVE-2022-0492 is explicitly called out in the article as a container-escape vulnerability whose root cause is improper privilege validation on the cgroups release_agent mechanism. The detection anchors on the exact filesystem object the exploit primitive must write to (release_agent + notify_on_release toggle) — there is no benign reason for a containerised workload to touch these files at runtime. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-0492
ATT&CKT1611 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has "/cgroup/" and (FileName == "release_agent" or FolderPath has "release_agent" or FileName == "notify_on_release")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has "/cgroup/" and (TargetFileName == "release_agent" or TargetFilePath has "release_agent" or TargetFileName == "notify_on_release")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Container Escape via cgroups release_agent Write (CVE-2022-0492)

[LLM] runC binary modified outside package manager (CVE-2019-5736 / CVE-2024-21626) Installation High
Detects writes to the runC binary on disk by anything other than the legitimate package-manager toolchain. The article calls out CVE-2019-5736 (runC binary overwrite from a compromised container via /proc/self/exe) and CVE-2024-21626 (runC fd handling for host fs access) — both leave the runC executable modified on the node. Rationale: Anchors on the exact runC binary paths and the package-manager exclusion list — CVE-2019-5736 is unique in that successful exploitation requires writing to the host's runC executable from a container context, so any modification of /usr/bin/runc outside the dpkg/yum/snap toolchain is overwhelmingly indicative of either supply-chain compromise or active runC exploit. Also catches the post-exploit cleanup phase of CVE-2024-21626. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2019-5736 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-21626
ATT&CKT1611 T1554
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath in~ ("/usr/bin/runc","/usr/sbin/runc","/usr/local/bin/runc","/usr/bin/docker-runc","/usr/libexec/docker/docker-runc") or FileName in~ ("runc","docker-runc")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/usr/bin","/usr/sbin","/usr/local/bin","/usr/libexec")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dpkg","apt","apt-get","yum","dnf","rpm","snap","snapd","zypper","containerd"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, ActionType, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath in~ ("/usr/bin/runc","/usr/sbin/runc","/usr/local/bin/runc","/usr/bin/docker-runc","/usr/libexec/docker/docker-runc")
| where not(ActingProcessName in~ ("dpkg","apt","apt-get","yum","dnf","rpm","snap","snapd","zypper","containerd"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, EventType, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Write to the runC executable on disk (/usr/bin/runc, /usr/sbin/runc, /usr/local/bin/runc, docker-runc variants) by a process that is not a known package manager. [LLM] Kubernetes API curl/wget with ServiceAccount token from container Actions on Objectives High
Detects the article's literal curl POST pattern against the Kubernetes API (`curl -k -X POST https://<kubernetes-url>/api/v1/namespaces/...`) and the canonical ServiceAccount token path. This is exactly the post-compromise behaviour described for the in-container malicious-actions vector — using the mounted /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token to talk to the cluster API. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article's verbatim Table 2 code block (`curl -k -X POST https://<kubernetes-url>/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods -H ...`) plus the canonical SA-token path the article explicitly calls out as automatically mounted and attacker-valuable. curl/wget shouldn't be hitting the API server in healthy pods — legitimate workloads use SDKs / kubectl.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1528 T1613
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("curl","wget","http","httpie")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/api/v1/namespaces","/api/v1/pods","/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token","kubernetes.default.svc",":6443/api/",":8443/api/v1/")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("kubelet","kubectl","helm","argocd","flux"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("curl","wget","http","httpie")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/api/v1/namespaces","/api/v1/pods","/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token","kubernetes.default.svc",":6443/api/",":8443/api/v1/")
| where not(ParentProcessName in~ ("kubelet","kubectl","helm","argocd","flux"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Kubernetes API curl/wget with ServiceAccount Token Path from Container
id: 1f9b0d4e-8a37-4c25-b6e9-3d1a5e7f2c48
description: curl / wget / httpie referencing the Kubernetes API server (/api/v1/namespaces, /api/v1/pods, kubernetes.default.svc, :6443/api) or the canonical ServiceAccount token path. The article quotes verbatim `curl -k -X POST https://<kubernetes-url>/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods -H "..."` as the in-container abuse pattern.
references:
    - https://securelist.com/container-attack-vectors/120010/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/01
tags:
    - attack.credential_access
    - attack.t1552.001
    - attack.t1528

logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: linux
detection:
    selection_bin:
        Image|endswith:
            - '/curl'
            - '/wget'
            - '/http'
            - '/httpie'
    selection_kube:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/api/v1/namespaces'
            - '/api/v1/pods'
            - '/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token'
            - 'kubernetes.default.svc'
            - ':6443/api/'
            - ':8443/api/v1/'
    filter_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '/kubelet'
            - '/kubectl'
            - '/helm'
            - '/argocd'
            - '/flux'
    condition: selection_bin and selection_kube and not filter_parent
falsepositives:
    - In-cluster operators that legitimately curl the API server with their SA token (Prometheus k8s-sd, custom controllers) — allow-list by image/namespace
    - Init containers that probe the API server during pod start-up
level: high

source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.executable.path:(*/curl OR */wget OR */http OR */httpie) @process.command_line:(*"/api/v1/namespaces"* OR *"/api/v1/pods"* OR *"/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token"* OR *"kubernetes.default.svc"* OR *":6443/api/"*) -@process.parent.executable.path:(*/kubelet OR */kubectl OR */helm OR */argocd OR */flux)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(curl|wget|http|httpie)$/i CommandLine=/(\/api\/v1\/(namespaces|pods)|\/var\/run\/secrets\/kubernetes\.io\/serviceaccount\/token|kubernetes\.default\.svc|:6443\/api\/|:8443\/api\/v1\/)/i
| NOT ParentBaseFileName=/^(kubelet|kubectl|helm|argocd|flux)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
# log group: /aws/eks/<cluster-name>/cluster
fields @timestamp, user.username, sourceIPs, verb, requestURI, userAgent, objectRef.resource, objectRef.namespace, responseStatus.code
| filter userAgent like /^(curl|Wget|HTTPie)/i
      and user.username like /system:serviceaccount:/
      and verb in ["create","get","list","patch","delete","watch"]
| sort @timestamp desc

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2019-5736", "CVE-2022-0492", "CVE-2024-21626")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId

| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1219
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'
            - '\NinjaOne.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - IT-approved RMM in use across the estate. Maintain a known-IT-
      tool exclusion list per environment.
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("94.154.172.43") or RemoteUrl has_any ("audit.checkmarx.cx")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |

    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba") or SHA1 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba") or MD5 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba") or SHA1 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba") or MD5 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.file_hash

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.process_hash IN ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba")

Article-specific behavioural hunt — Containers on fire: from container escapes to supply chain attacks Installation High
Auto-generated hunt targeting the specific binaries, paths, registry locations and command-line fragments named in this article. Hunting tier — needs analyst review and environment tuning before promotion to alerting.
ATT&CKT1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
// Article-specific bespoke detection — Containers on fire: from container escapes to supply chain attacks
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("/dev/tcp/", "/usr/local/sbin", "/usr/local/bin", "/usr/sbin", "/usr/bin"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

Miasma supply chain attack: malicious code found in @redhat-cloud-services npm packages

Snyk
2026-06-01 4 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

A supply chain worm dubbed Miasma has been found in dozens of @redhat-cloud-services npm releases. The malicious preinstall hook steals credentials, probes cloud identities, and can republish other packages.

ATT&CKT1027 T1190 T1195.002 T1555.003

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Miasma supply chain attack: malicious code found in @redhat-cloud-services npm p
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05
status: experimental
description: |
    User-driven consent to a third-party OAuth application — illicit-
    consent attack precursor. Pair with first-time-seen-app heuristic
    in your SIEM for higher fidelity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1528
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    product: azure
    service: auditlogs
detection:
    selection:
        OperationName: 'Consent to application'
        Result: 'success'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate first-time SaaS app onboarding
level: medium
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")

[LLM] npm install of dependency-confusion scoped packages (moika.tech actor) Delivery High
Detects npm/node executing install lifecycle hooks for any of the nine attacker-controlled organizational scopes published by mr.4nd3r50n, ce-rwb, and t-in-one on 2026-05-28/29. The scope strings appear in the resolution command line during npm install, making this a high-fidelity early-stage signal. Rationale: Anchored on the nine attacker-controlled npm scopes named in the article (@cloudplatform-single-spa, @wb-track, @data-science, @ce-rwb, @payments-widget, @travel-autotests, @t-in-one, @capibar.chat, @sber-ecom-core) — these are not real internal namespaces, so any developer-host hit is by definition an unwanted install.

[LLM] C2 callback to moika.tech payload distribution infrastructure Command & Control High
Detects outbound HTTPS from any process to oob.moika.tech or the parent moika.tech domain — the dropper fetches its platform-specific payload from https://oob.moika.tech/payload/{win|mac|linux}. Catches the post-install reconnaissance stager regardless of which scope triggered it. Rationale: oob.moika.tech (and the parent moika.tech) is the single C2 endpoint named in the article — every package in the cluster fetches https://oob.moika.tech/payload/<platform>. Domain has no legitimate dev-tooling use and was first seen in this campaign on 2026-05-28.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("oob.moika.tech","moika.tech")
   or RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)moika\.tech/payload/(win|mac|linux)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where DestinationHostName has_any ("oob.moika.tech","moika.tech")
         or RequestURL has_any ("oob.moika.tech","moika.tech/payload/")
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceHostName, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor),
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where Name has "moika.tech"

  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where HttpHostName has_any ("oob.moika.tech","moika.tech") or Url has "moika.tech/payload/"
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, HttpHostName, Url, HttpMethod, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Malicious postinstall.js dropped under node_modules for actor scopes Installation High
Detects the obfuscated ~7 KB postinstall.js stager being materialised inside node_modules/@<actor-scope>/<pkg>/scripts/postinstall.js. Hunting tier because file-event volume from npm installs is high — the value is in retrospective hunts and forensic timeline reconstruction. Rationale: The article specifies `scripts/postinstall.js` as the obfuscated stager, dropped under each malicious scoped package. Pairing the literal filename with the actor's nine scope strings inside node_modules yields a near-zero-FP file event because no legitimate package would publish under these namespaces.

[LLM] node.exe spawns detached child from tmpdir after npm install (moika.tech dropper) Installation Medium
After fetching the platform payload, the obfuscated stager writes it to the OS tmpdir and spawns a detached child. Detects node.exe spawning a process whose image lives in %TEMP% / %TMP% / /tmp where the grandparent chain involves npm — catches stage-2 even if the C2 domain rotates. Rationale: Article describes the deobfuscated execution flow: stager fetches payload from oob.moika.tech, writes it to tmpdir, then spawns a detached child. Constraining node.exe parent + tmpdir child path + correlation with a recent npm install on the same host turns a noisy primitive (node spawning anything) into a campaign-specific signal.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1105 T1564.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let NpmHosts = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd")
        or ProcessCommandLine has "npm install"
    | project DeviceId, NpmTime = Timestamp;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where FolderPath has_any (
    @"\AppData\Local\Temp\",
    @"\Windows\Temp\",
    "/tmp/",
    "/var/folders/")
| where FileName !in~ ("conhost.exe","node.exe")
| join kind=inner NpmHosts on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (NpmTime .. NpmTime + 30m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          NpmTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, NpmTime)
| order by Timestamp desc

    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\npm.cmd" or NewProcessName endswith "\\npm.exe" or CommandLine has "npm install"
    | project Computer, NpmTime = TimeGenerated;

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count

        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count

    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |

    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

            - 'FromBase64String'

            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'

            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'

level: high

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: PATCH /workspaces/{id}/members/{user_id} role-change request Exploitation High
Hunts the core privilege-escalation primitive in CVE-2026-47416 — an HTTP PATCH against /workspaces/<workspace_id>/members/<user_id> on praisonai-platform <=0.1.2. Because require_workspace_member defaults to min_role='member' and the route never overrides it, any authenticated member can write {"role":"owner"} to any member row. Outside of one-off legitimate owner-driven role tweaks this URL+verb pair is extremely rare, so even URI-only telemetry is high-fidelity for affected deployments. Rationale: Article pinpoints the exact endpoint shape (PATCH /workspaces/{workspace_id}/members/{user_id}) and the route file (api/routes/workspaces.py:115-127). Even without request-body visibility, the verb+path pair is rare enough on praisonai-platform to be high-fidelity; restricting on HTTP 2xx removes 401/403 noise from unaffected versions. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory body and corroborated by independent PraisonAI security coverage on cybersecuritynews.com and Sysdig confirming the platform's pattern of weakly-gated workspace endpoints. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2m8-4gcg-v22g • https://cybersecuritynews.com/praisonai-vulnerability-exploited/ • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/cve-2026-44338-praisonai-authentication-bypass-in-under-4-hours-and-the-growing-trend-of-rapid-exploitation
ATT&CKT1068 T1190 T1098

| where HttpMethod =~ "PATCH"
| where Url matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/[^/?#]+"
| where HttpStatusCode in ("200","204")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, HttpMethod, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestBodyBytes, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DstHostname
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416 PATCH workspaces members role-change
id: 7a4cbf8e-2b39-4b9a-a4ba-2026474160c1
status: experimental
description: Detects HTTP PATCH requests against the praisonai-platform /workspaces/{workspace_id}/members/{user_id} endpoint that exposes a vertical privilege-escalation primitive (CVE-2026-47416). The endpoint should normally see near-zero PATCH traffic; any successful PATCH is suspicious until the deployment is patched to >=0.1.3 with the min_role='owner' gate applied.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2m8-4gcg-v22g
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/30
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1098
  - cve.2026.47416
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection_method:
    cs-method: 'PATCH'
  selection_uri:
    cs-uri-stem|re: '(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/[^/?#]+$'
  selection_status:
    sc-status:
      - 200
      - 204
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate workspace owner changing another member's role via the official UI (will be rare and identifiable by the originating account being an existing owner)
  - Internal admin scripts that pre-seed workspace ownership during tenant provisioning
level: high
@http.method:PATCH @http.url_details.path:*/workspaces/*/members/* @http.status_code:(200 OR 204) (service:praisonai-platform OR service:praisonai OR @service:praisonai*)
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.status) as statuses values(Web.user) as users from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method=PATCH Web.url="*/workspaces/*/members/*" by Web.src Web.user Web.dest Web.http_user_agent | rename Web.* as * | regex url="/workspaces/[^/]+/members/[^/?#]+" | where statuses="200" OR statuses="204" | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.status) as statuses values(Web.user) as users from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method=PATCH Web.url="*/workspaces/*/members/*" by Web.src Web.user Web.dest Web.http_user_agent | rename Web.* as * | regex url="/workspaces/[^/]+/members/[^/?#]+" | where statuses="200" OR statuses="204" | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: Member self-promotion + legitimate-owner demotion chain within one hour Installation High
Catches the two-request takeover chain described in the advisory — the attacker first self-promotes (PATCH on their own user_id with {"role":"owner"}) and then demotes the legitimate owner (PATCH on the owner's user_id with {"role":"member"}). This temporal pivot is much higher fidelity than UC1 because legitimate workspace operations almost never produce two role-mutating PATCHs from the same client IP within a short window. Rationale: The advisory explicitly calls out the two-PATCH primitive: 'owner lockout in two requests total'. Workspaces where the same client IP/user mutates 2+ distinct member rows within the hour is a behaviour the legitimate UI essentially never produces — owners normally change one role at a time and rarely demote themselves seconds after promoting. Threshold of >=2 distinct TargetUser within 60m is the article's own attack cadence. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2m8-4gcg-v22g
ATT&CKT1098 T1531 T1136.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let Lookback = 7d;
let WindowMin = 60m;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where HttpMethod =~ "PATCH"
| where Url matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/[^/?#]+"
| where HttpStatusCode in ("200","204")
| extend Workspace = extract(@"(?i)/workspaces/([^/]+)/members/", 1, Url)
| extend TargetUser = extract(@"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/([^/?#]+)", 1, Url)
| summarize PatchCount = count(),
            TargetsTouched = dcount(TargetUser),
            Targets = make_set(TargetUser, 10),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Workspace, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where PatchCount >= 2 and TargetsTouched >= 2   // self-promote + owner-demote = 2 distinct user_ids
| extend WindowMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| order by FirstSeen desc
@http.method:PATCH @http.url_details.path:*/workspaces/*/members/* @http.status_code:(200 OR 204) (service:praisonai-platform OR service:praisonai OR @service:praisonai*)
WEB

| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.status) as statuses min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method=PATCH Web.url="*/workspaces/*/members/*" Web.status IN (200,204) by Web.src Web.user _time span=1h | rename Web.* as * | where count >= 2 | eval windowMinutes=round((lastSeen-firstSeen)/60,1) | where windowMinutes <= 60 | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | `security_content_ctime(firstSeen)` | `security_content_ctime(lastSeen)`
[LLM] praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: Bulk agent/issue/project/comment enumeration immediately after a workspace role-change PATCH Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the collection phase of the takeover chain — once the attacker holds owner via the CVE-2026-47416 primitive they pivot into LIST endpoints (agents, issues, projects, comments) that were previously gated by owner-tier access. The detection joins a successful PATCH on /workspaces/*/members/* with a burst of GET/LIST traffic from the same session within 15 minutes, flagging the post-elevation data harvest. Rationale: Article explicitly chains the elevation into 'exfiltrate everything via the agent/issue/project/comment IDORs that were filed as separate advisories'. The named LIST endpoints come from the advisory's own corroboration section. Pairing the elevation event with the post-elevation enumeration inside 15 minutes weeds out generic browse traffic from a non-attack owner. Burst threshold of 10 distinct GETs is calibrated to the article's described mass-pull behaviour rather than a casual single-resource read. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2m8-4gcg-v22g
ATT&CKT1213 T1530 T1087.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let Lookback = 7d;
let PostWindow = 15m;
let BurstThreshold = 10;   // 10+ list calls inside 15m post-PATCH = harvest-shaped
let RoleChanges = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where HttpMethod =~ "PATCH"
    | where Url matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/[^/?#]+"
    | where HttpStatusCode in ("200","204")
    | project PatchTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, PatchedWorkspace = extract(@"(?i)/workspaces/([^/]+)/members/", 1, Url);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where HttpMethod =~ "GET"
| where Url matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/(agents|issues|projects|comments)"
| join kind=inner RoleChanges on SrcIpAddr
| where TimeGenerated between (PatchTime .. PatchTime + PostWindow)
| summarize ListCount = count(),
            DistinctResources = dcount(extract(@"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/(agents|issues|projects|comments)", 1, Url)),
            ListUrls = make_set(Url, 25),
            FirstList = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastList = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, PatchedWorkspace, PatchTime
| where ListCount >= BurstThreshold
| extend DelaySeconds = datetime_diff('second', FirstList, PatchTime)
| order by PatchTime desc

[LLM] Vulnerable praisonai-platform deployment hunt (uvicorn launching praisonai_platform.api.app) Installation High
Surfaces hosts running praisonai-platform — the vulnerable component in CVE-2026-47410. Defaults bypass the secret-guard when PLATFORM_ENV is unset (its default is 'dev'), so any deployment started without explicitly exporting PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET is exploitable. This UC identifies the population that needs urgent remediation before attackers find them on Shodan. Rationale: Pivots on the exact startup invocation named in the advisory (`uvicorn praisonai_platform.api.app:app`) and the package import name. The `--reload` exclusion drops developer workstations where the dev server is intentional. The SecretInCmdLine/ProdEnvInCmdLine extends help the analyst decide remediation urgency at triage time without a second query.
ATT&CKT1190 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "uvicorn"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("praisonai_platform.api.app", "praisonai_platform", "praisonai-platform")
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has "--reload")              // dev-mode flag, common on developer workstations
| extend SecretInCmdLine = ProcessCommandLine has "PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET"
| extend ProdEnvInCmdLine = ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)PLATFORM_ENV\s*=\s*(prod|production|stage|staging)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          SecretInCmdLine, ProdEnvInCmdLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] praisonai-platform cross-tenant workspace operations from single source IP Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects JWT-forgery exploitation against CVE-2026-47410. After minting a token with arbitrary 'sub', the attacker hits authenticated routes — /auth/me to validate, then POST /workspaces/{id}/members, PATCH /workspaces/{id}, or DELETE /workspaces/{id} across multiple distinct workspace UUIDs. Catches the post-forgery pivot where one IP authenticates as many different user_ids in a short window — a pattern legitimate users do not produce. Rationale: Anchors on the exact route shapes the advisory's exploit chain calls out (steps 5-6: /auth/me + cross-workspace POST/PATCH/DELETE). The 'distinct workspaces >= 3 within 30m from one source IP' threshold captures the asymmetry between a legitimate user (their own 1-2 workspaces) and a forger pivoting across tenants. Falcon LogScale and CloudWatch left empty because FDR doesn't ship app-tier HTTP request logs and the CloudTrail/VPC schema doesn't carry the request path; this detection genuinely needs reverse-proxy/WAF telemetry the host SIEM aggregates.
ATT&CKT1078 T1190 T1212
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Best-effort proxy via inbound network telemetry — true detection lives in web logs (see sentinel_kql).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("praisonai_platform", "praisonai-platform") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "uvicorn"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| summarize InboundCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), DistinctPorts = dcount(LocalPort)
   by DeviceName, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName
| where InboundCount > 50
| order by InboundCount desc
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let WorkspaceRegex = @"/workspaces/([0-9a-f\-]{8,})";
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where RequestURL has_any ("/auth/me", "/auth/register", "/workspaces/")
| extend Method = toupper(coalesce(RequestMethod, DeviceCustomString1))
| extend WorkspaceId = extract(WorkspaceRegex, 1, RequestURL)
| extend IsDestructive = Method in ("DELETE", "PATCH") or (Method == "POST" and RequestURL has "/members")
| extend IsAuthMe = RequestURL has "/auth/me"
| extend IsRegister = RequestURL has "/auth/register"
| summarize
    AuthMeHits = countif(IsAuthMe),
    RegisterHits = countif(IsRegister),
    DistinctWorkspaces = dcountif(WorkspaceId, isnotempty(WorkspaceId)),
    DestructiveOps = countif(IsDestructive),
    SampleWorkspaces = make_set_if(WorkspaceId, isnotempty(WorkspaceId), 10),
    SampleURLs = make_set(RequestURL, 15),
    Methods = make_set(Method, 10),
    FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
    by SourceIP, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMinutes)
| where DistinctWorkspaces >= 3 and DestructiveOps >= 1   // 3 = empirical: a real user touches their own 1-2 workspaces; cross-tenant pivot starts at 3+
| order by LastSeen desc
@http.url_details.path:("/auth/me" OR *"/workspaces/"* OR "/auth/register") @http.method:(DELETE OR PATCH OR POST) -@http.useragent:(*HealthCheck* OR *k6* OR *Locust* OR *Prometheus*)

[LLM] PraisonAI Platform member role mutation endpoint hit (CVE-2026-47407 privilege escalation) Actions on Objectives High
Hunts HTTP PATCH/POST/DELETE calls against /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/members[/{user_id}] on PraisonAI Platform. Per CVE-2026-47407, these routes inherit the default `min_role="member"` so any basic member can promote themselves to admin/owner, demote/remove other members, or delete the workspace. Any hit on these endpoints by a non-owner principal is high-fidelity for exploitation. Rationale: Article explicitly names routes/workspaces.py:115-141 update_member_role / add_member / remove_member / delete_workspace as the buggy member-management endpoints; any non-admin caller hitting them is exploit-shaped. Pattern is the FastAPI prefix /api/v1/workspaces/{uuid}/members[/{uuid}] taken directly from the affected-functionality table in the GHSA.
ATT&CKT1078 T1098 T1548
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let LookbackDays = 7d;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where HttpMethod in ("PATCH","POST","DELETE")
| where Url matches regex @"/api/v1/workspaces/[0-9a-f-]{36}/members(?:/[0-9a-f-]{36})?/?$"
| where HttpStatusCode between (200 .. 299)
| extend url_workspace_id = extract(@"/api/v1/workspaces/([0-9a-f-]{36})/members", 1, Url),
         target_user_id  = extract(@"/members/([0-9a-f-]{36})", 1, Url)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, HttpMethod, Url,
          url_workspace_id, target_user_id, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DstHostname
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] PraisonAI Platform cross-workspace nested-resource enumeration (CVE-2026-47407 IDOR) Actions on Objectives High
Hunts a single authenticated user repeatedly hitting nested-resource routes (/agents/{id}, /issues/{id}, /projects/{id}, /labels/{id}, /dependencies/...) under one workspace prefix while supplying many distinct inner UUIDs. CVE-2026-47407's IDOR pattern requires the attacker to keep their own workspace_id in the URL and rotate the inner resource UUID; this enumeration shape is the exploit fingerprint and cannot be produced by normal single-workspace usage at any meaningful rate. Rationale: Article's PoC step 6 explicitly shows GET /api/v1/workspaces/{Mallory_ws}/agents/{Alice_agent_id} succeeding cross-tenant — the exploit fingerprint is many distinct inner_id under a single (or pair of) workspace_id prefix(es). Article enumerates the exact resource_kind set (agents/issues/projects/labels/dependencies in the affected-routes table). Threshold (15 distinct in 10m, ≤2 url workspaces) targets the enumeration shape rather than per-request lookup.
ATT&CKT1190 T1213 T1530
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let LookbackHours = 24h;
let WindowMinutes = 10m;
let MinDistinctInnerIds = 15;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
| where HttpMethod in ("GET","PATCH","DELETE")
| where Url matches regex @"/api/v1/workspaces/[0-9a-f-]{36}/(agents|issues|projects|labels|dependencies)/[0-9a-f-]{36}"
| extend url_workspace_id = extract(@"/api/v1/workspaces/([0-9a-f-]{36})", 1, Url),
         resource_kind   = extract(@"/(agents|issues|projects|labels|dependencies)/[0-9a-f-]{36}", 1, Url),
         inner_id        = extract(@"/(?:agents|issues|projects|labels|dependencies)/([0-9a-f-]{36})", 1, Url)
| summarize distinct_inner_ids   = dcount(inner_id),
            distinct_workspaces  = dcount(url_workspace_id),
            hits                 = count(),
            kinds                = make_set(resource_kind, 10),
            first_seen           = min(TimeGenerated),
            last_seen            = max(TimeGenerated)
          by SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMinutes)
// 15 = empirical: a normal user rarely opens >15 distinct agents/issues in 10m; IDOR-style enumeration easily exceeds it
| where distinct_inner_ids >= MinDistinctInnerIds and distinct_workspaces <= 2
| order by distinct_inner_ids desc
@http.method:(GET OR PATCH OR DELETE) @http.url_details.path:(*/api/v1/workspaces/*/agents/* OR */api/v1/workspaces/*/issues/* OR */api/v1/workspaces/*/projects/* OR */api/v1/workspaces/*/labels/* OR */api/v1/workspaces/*/dependencies/*) @http.status_code:[200 TO 299]
# log group: /aws/elasticloadbalancing/<alb-name>
fields @timestamp, client_ip, request_verb, request_url, target_status_code
| filter request_url like /\/api\/v1\/workspaces\/[0-9a-f-]+\/(agents|issues|projects|labels|dependencies)\/[0-9a-f-]+/
      and request_verb in ["GET", "PATCH", "DELETE"]
      and target_status_code >= 200
      and target_status_code < 300
| parse request_url /\/workspaces\/(?<url_ws>[0-9a-f-]+)\/(?<kind>agents|issues|projects|labels|dependencies)\/(?<inner_id>[0-9a-f-]+)/
| stats count(*) as hits, count_distinct(inner_id) as distinct_inner_ids, count_distinct(url_ws) as distinct_workspaces by client_ip, bin(10m)
| filter distinct_inner_ids >= 15 and distinct_workspaces <= 2
| sort distinct_inner_ids desc

[LLM] PraisonAI Platform open-registration burst followed by workspace privileged action Delivery High
Hunts the bootstrap pattern in CVE-2026-47407 / GHSA-h8q5-cp56-rr65: anonymous POST /api/v1/auth/register succeeds (open registration with no email verification) and within minutes the same source IP / new account starts touching member-management or cross-workspace nested-resource routes. Catches automated exploitation kits and attacker-from-the-internet abuse of the 0.0.0.0:8000 default bind. Rationale: Article calls out `/api/v1/auth/register` as open + no email verification (routes/auth.py:19-29) and the default 0.0.0.0:8000 bind (__main__.py:13-16) — the GHSA explicitly states "one curl from any unauthenticated network position is enough to bootstrap into the system." Pairing a register success with sensitive nested-route activity from the same source IP within 10 minutes is the exact bootstrap-to-abuse pivot.
ATT&CKT1190 T1136 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSeconds = 600;
let Register = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where HttpMethod == "POST"
    | where Url has "/api/v1/auth/register"
    | where HttpStatusCode between (200 .. 299)
    | project RegisterTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, RegisterUserAgent = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where HttpMethod in ("PATCH","POST","DELETE")
| where Url matches regex @"/api/v1/workspaces/[0-9a-f-]{36}/(members(/[0-9a-f-]{36})?|agents/[0-9a-f-]{36}|projects/[0-9a-f-]{36}|issues/[0-9a-f-]{36}|labels/[0-9a-f-]{36})/?$"
| where HttpStatusCode between (200 .. 299)
| join kind=inner Register on SrcIpAddr
| where TimeGenerated between (RegisterTime .. RegisterTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| project RegisterTime, SensitiveTime = TimeGenerated,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, RegisterTime),
          SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, HttpMethod, Url, HttpStatusCode, RegisterUserAgent
| order by SensitiveTime desc
@http.method:POST @http.url_details.path:*/api/v1/auth/register @http.status_code:[200 TO 299]
# log group: /aws/elasticloadbalancing/<alb-name>
fields @timestamp, client_ip, request_verb, request_url, target_status_code, user_agent
| filter request_url like /\/api\/v1\/auth\/register/
      and request_verb = "POST"
      and target_status_code >= 200
      and target_status_code < 300
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 200

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-47407")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-47407")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

DeviceProcessEvents

DeviceFileEvents
